evidence.effect_or_condition: acute cognition, mood, and well-being in healthy participants
evidence.study_type: systematic review of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: healthy participants in acute taurine supplementation trials
evidence.sample_size: 8 randomized controlled trials; 244 participants; all eligible trials were acute single-dose studies
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 systematic review of eight randomized trials found that acute taurine produced at most small and inconsistent cognitive effects, with most cognitive outcomes showing no effect. Trials combining taurine with caffeine showed more consistent performance signals, but they cannot establish taurine-alone efficacy.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review; acute-only; mostly null or inconsistent
evidence.safety_note: All eligible trials were acute single-dose studies, so the review does not establish chronic cognitive benefit or long-term safety. Habitual diet and baseline sulphur-amino-acid status were not characterized. Two review authors reported unrelated taurine research funding from Viridian Nutrition; the funder was reported to have no role in the review.

evidence.effect_or_condition: cognition and anterior-cingulate neurometabolites in alcohol use disorder
evidence.population: adults with moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder
evidence.sample_size: 23 adults; NAC n=9, placebo n=14; mean follow-up about 19 days
evidence.supported_claim_language: In a very small randomized trial in adults with moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder, NAC did not significantly improve Stroop or Trail Making performance and did not significantly change the measured anterior-cingulate GSH/Cr, tNAAG/Cr, or Glu/Cr ratios versus placebo.
evidence.evidence_grade: small randomized trial; preliminary null evidence
evidence.safety_note: The study was very small and short, in a specific alcohol-use-disorder population. The studied 2400 mg/day exposure is trial context only and should not be converted into a consumer dose or generalized to healthy cognition.

evidence.effect_or_condition: craving, withdrawal symptoms, and short-term adverse events in substance-use disorders
evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: participants with substance-use disorders across randomized NAC trials
evidence.sample_size: 11 randomized trials contributed to the craving analysis
evidence.supported_claim_language: A meta-analysis of randomized NAC trials in substance-use disorders found a statistically significant craving signal (SMD -0.61, 95% CI -1.17 to -0.06), but heterogeneity was very high (I²=85%) and the authors characterized the evidence as weak. Withdrawal symptoms were not significantly improved.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; weak evidence with high heterogeneity
evidence.safety_note: Short-term side effects and dropouts did not differ significantly from control in the pooled analysis, which does not establish long-term safety. Substance type, population, regimen, and treatment context varied across studies.

evidence.effect_or_condition: depressive symptoms in major depressive disorder
evidence.population: patients with diagnosed major depressive disorder
evidence.supported_claim_language: A recent synthesis of 13 studies in 710 patients with major depressive disorder reported a pooled depressive-symptom signal favoring probiotics (SMD 0.38), but moderate heterogeneity remained and subgroup or meta-regression analyses did not identify a clear moderator.
evidence.safety_note: Strain, combination, regimen, treatment context, and population differences remain unresolved. The result does not support a universal class effect for every probiotic product or strain.

evidence.population: people with depression receiving probiotic supplementation
evidence.sample_size: 13 studies in the review; 7 studies in the meta-analysis
evidence.supported_claim_language: A recent review found a pooled depressive-symptom improvement signal with probiotics in people with depression, while pooled IL-6 and TNF-α outcomes were not significantly changed. The clinical signal therefore should not be presented as proof that an anti-inflammatory mechanism caused the symptom change.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; mixed clinical and biomarker findings
evidence.safety_note: The evidence spans differing strains and regimens and does not establish interchangeability across probiotic products. Null inflammatory-biomarker findings must remain visible alongside the symptom signal.

evidence.effect_or_condition: cognitive outcomes in mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer disease, or dementia
evidence.population: older adults with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer disease, or dementia
evidence.sample_size: 9 studies; 617 patients in the MMSE analysis
evidence.supported_claim_language: A recent ginseng meta-analysis in cognitively impaired older adults found small statistically favorable changes on MMSE and ADAS-Cog, but the review characterized the magnitude as modest and not reaching a threshold for clinical significance.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; statistically positive but clinically modest
evidence.safety_note: The evidence is population-specific and does not establish a generic nootropic effect in healthy adults. Preparation, dose, duration, study count, and heterogeneity limit interpretation; subgroup doses are study context, not consumer recommendations.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: people with subjective memory impairment, mild cognitive impairment, or Alzheimer disease
evidence.supported_claim_language: Across eight randomized trials in people with subjective memory impairment, mild cognitive impairment, or Alzheimer disease, pooled MMSE and ADAS-Cog results favored ginseng, but MMSE heterogeneity was substantial and the review called for further work on long-term effects and dosage.
evidence.safety_note: The findings do not establish an optimal long-term regimen and should not be generalized to healthy-user cognitive enhancement. Preparation and subgroup definitions must remain explicit.

evidence.effect_or_condition: mental fatigue, visuo-cognitive processing, perceived exertion, and strength performance
evidence.supported_claim_language: A small four-day crossover trial found only trivial-to-small effects of Rhodiola rosea on mental fatigue, visuo-cognitive processing, and perceived exertion. Selected strength outcomes favored Rhodiola, but most of 52 comparisons were trivial, so the study does not support a broad acute cognition or anti-fatigue claim.
evidence.evidence_grade: small randomized crossover trial; mostly trivial-to-small effects
evidence.safety_note: The sample was only 18 young healthy participants and exposure lasted four days. Several authors reported scientific-advisor relationships with sports-supplement or ingredient companies; the finding should remain short-term and context-specific.

evidence.effect_or_condition: blood pressure in adults with prehypertension or hypertension
evidence.supported_claim_language: A three-study meta-analysis reported a pooled systolic blood-pressure reduction of 6.03 mmHg, but heterogeneity was high (I²=82%). The pooled diastolic change was not statistically significant because its confidence interval crossed zero.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; small evidence base with high systolic heterogeneity
evidence.safety_note: Only three studies met eligibility and trial quality varied. A favorable 1000 mg/day subgroup is study context, not a consumer dose recommendation. No serious symptoms in the included studies does not establish long-term safety.

evidence.population: gastrointestinal-cancer survivors at least four months after treatment with moderate-to-severe cancer-related fatigue
evidence.supported_claim_language: In a randomized four-week trial of 65 gastrointestinal-cancer survivors with clinically meaningful cancer-related fatigue, standardized Panax ginseng extract reduced fatigue severity versus placebo and improved selected activity, walking, mood, and enjoyment-of-life interference measures.
evidence.evidence_grade: randomized controlled trial; population-specific supportive-care evidence
evidence.safety_note: No treatment-related adverse events were reported, but the study was small and only four weeks long, so it cannot establish long-term or rare-event safety. The studied 250 mg/day extract exposure is trial context only and should not be generalized to generic tiredness or healthy-user energy.
